Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Orchid renewal — initial ask (term change + evidence)

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the call earlier. We are preparing the PO for the renewal but our procurement & legal teams have three items they need cleared before we can route to finance:

1) Term length: Orchid prefers a 12-month renewal vs the 24-month term your AE noted. Would Redwood be open to 12 months for this renewal?
2) Liability/Cap: our legal proposes a higher cap for data breach carveouts (we can share suggested language) — want to understand Redwood's flexibility.
3) Evidence: attached is our intake — we need Redwood's latest SOC 2 attestation and a confirmation of data residency for EU / US data segmentation.

I attached our proposed order form (Orchid_Proposed_OrderForm_2028-07-09.pdf) with line items for the pilot expansion and a PO placeholder. Can you loop in legal and let me know a timeline for redlines?

Best,
Mike

Head of Procurement | Orchid Health
procurement@orchidhealth.com

Cc: Mike Carter <m.carter@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Orchid renewal — initial ask (term change + evidence)

Kimberly / Tessa — forwarding Orchid's ask. Quick triage:

- Term: they want 12 months instead of 24. This is an upsell but they want shorter commitment. From GTM perspective, they are expanding usage (+30% pilot). Recommend we accept 12 months for the pilot cohort if we keep standard pricing and add a committed uplift clause for month-to-month after the pilot.
- Liability: Mike flagged a higher cap request for breach carveouts. Please advise whether we can accept a carveout cap increase for this account or propose alternative language (liability cap tied to the most recent 12 months' fees).
- Evidence: they requested SOC2 — attaching the SOC2 we have (SOC2_Attestation_2027.pdf) and my suggested MSA markup (Redwood_MSA_v3_markedup.docx).

Can you review the attached MSA markup and call out must-have legal changes vs negotiable commercial asks? If we can finalize redlines by EOD Friday I will send updated order form back to Mike and include DocuSign link.

Thanks —
Vanessa
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_Attestation_2027.pdf; Redwood_MSA_v3_markedup.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Orchid renewal — initial ask (term change + evidence)

Vanessa / Tessa — reviewed Orchid's proposed order form and your markup. Key legal positions and suggestions below (high-level):

1) Term length: we can accommodate a 12-month term for the renewal as a commercial concession tied to the pilot expansion, provided we include an explicit clause that any subsequent month-to-month usage is billed at the higher list rate unless a new commitment is signed. Add a committed-uplift exhibit (Exhibit C) that defines thresholds and pricing steps.

2) Liability cap / carveouts: Our standard approach is liability cap = greater of $X or 12 months' fees. For security incident carveouts, we will not accept an unlimited or materially higher cap. Propose alternative language: security breach carveout limited to 12 months' fees plus direct remediation costs (no punitive or consequential damages). If they push higher, we request a trade — e.g., additional indemnity language or a minimum term.

3) Data residency: we confirm Redwood can segregate logs by region if requested; however, full data residency guarantees for derived embeddings may require Dedicated or Private deployment. Recommend we confirm "data processed and stored in the US" for Orchid's primary tenant and note options for EU residency in Exhibit B.

4) SOC2: attached attestation is fine. We'll provide the control summary; do not send system-level logs.

Next steps: I've attached MSA_legal_comments_v3.docx with line-item legal edits (redlines and rationale). Vanessa, if you want to accept the term concession, I recommend we: (a) finalize Exhibit C (commitment/uptick pricing), (b) hold on increasing the liability cap, and (c) offer a compromise on data residency language with a path to Dedicated if Orchid requires hard guarantees.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_legal_comments_v3.docx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mike Carter <m.carter@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchid renewal — MSA + order form (our compromise)

Mike — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per legal review, Redwood can accept the 12-month term for this renewal tied to the pilot expansion under the following commercial/legal package: 

- Term: 12 months for the renewal term in the attached OrderForm_Final_ExhibitC.xlsx (pilot cohort pricing and thresholds).
- Pricing/Uplift: month-to-month post-pilot will be at list rates unless a new commitment is signed; Exhibit C defines staging and price breakpoints.
- Liability: Redwood cannot raise the security carveout to an uncapped level. We propose liability cap = greater of $250,000 or 12 months' fees; for security events, we will cover direct remediation costs plus 12 months' fees.
- Data residency: we confirm processing/storage in the US for Orchid's tenant. If Orchid requires EU residency guarantees, that will require Dedicated/Private (we included language in Exhibit B to cover the migration path).

I've attached a clean order form and the redlineed MSA with legal's comments. If Orchid accepts, we can route to DocuSign (link below) and finance will prepare for PO. Please let me know by EOD Monday so we can meet procurement timelines.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_Final_ExhibitC.xlsx; Redwood_MSA_v3_markedup.docx
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-orchid-msa

Subject: Re: Orchid renewal — MSA + order form (our compromise)

Vanessa / Kimberly — appreciate the clear summary. A few points from Orchid's side:

- Term: We can accept 12 months if Redwood agrees to a 30-day pilot clause that allows Orchid to expand the pilot cohort within the first 60 days at the agreed pilot pricing band in Exhibit C. After 60 days, month-to-month rates apply unless committed.
- Liability: Orchid Legal is reluctant on the flat $250k cap for security carveouts. They asked whether Redwood will consider a cap equal to 6 months' fees for security incidents. If Redwood cannot, they want a more explicit remediation SLA and a credits mechanism.
- Evidence: SOC2 attachment received and underwriting ok. Can you confirm the control summary will be shared with our security team only?

I can accept the DocuSign flow once we iron the days on the pilot clause and the liability language. Sending a placeholder PO in case that helps speed Finance.

Thanks,
Mike
